### Butte-Silver Bow

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟡 Pending
- **Recorded date:** —

- **Duration:** Earlier reporting described a proposed six-month moratorium with up to two one-year extensions, followed by permanent regulations; the underlying historical source is not retained. An October 28 secondary account likewise describes a proposed six-month moratorium. The enacted term, if any, is unverified.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `mt-butte-silver-bow-undated`
- **Authority and source:** Council motion introduced by Commissioner Michele Shea directing the county attorney to prepare a temporary data-center moratorium, reported adopted 11-0 on 2026-09-02. A secondary report identifies proposed council bill 2026-03 on 2026-10-28; its text and official status are unverified.
- **What prompted it:** Ongoing local debate over data center development, including a separately litigated local ballot initiative (406 People First / Local Initiative 00-02) to require voter approval of data centers, a pending Montana Supreme Court appeal over that initiative's ballot eligibility, and public testimony citing power-supply concerns tied to a still-pending Montana Public Service Commission large-load tariff proceeding.
- **Affected projects:** News coverage references a company exploring potential data center sites in Silver Bow County (behind the ballot-initiative and moratorium debate), but no specific named project or MW figure was located in captured sources.
- **Status notes:** Pending as of 2026-09-23, when the reported September 2 council vote directed the county attorney to prepare a moratorium. A later Citizen Portal account dated 2026-10-28 reports that the Committee of the Whole held proposed council bill 2026-03 in abeyance by a 12-0 vote and returned it for drafting; the account is gated and the official action was not independently established. The earlier review reported a district-court ruling against the citizen group, a Montana Supreme Court appeal and temporary permission for the initiative to remain alive; it also cited a related report that the initiative was ultimately kept off the November 2026 ballot. Those litigation details have not been reverified here. [VERIFY: proposed instrument and official action, any adoption or later changes, and current legal status.]
- **Outcome:** Council voted 11-0 on 2026-09-02 to direct preparation of a proposed moratorium. A secondary October 28 account reports that proposed council bill 2026-03 was held in abeyance for further drafting; later action and adoption remain unverified.

- **Policy ID:** `mt-hb263-lc0636`

- **Status:** Died in process (tabled in House committee 2025-02-03, missed general bill transmittal deadline 2025-03-12), 2025-05-20
- **Provisions:** Would have revised digital asset mining and data center ratemaking laws. Captured bill-status records identify the proposal as data center electricity reporting and ratemaking legislation; not a moratorium bill.

### HB424 / LC3009

- **Policy ID:** `mt-hb424-lc3009`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Katie Zolnikov; R
- **Status:** Signed by Governor 2025-05-13, Chapter 678 assigned 2025-05-19
- **Provisions:** Revises Class 17 data center property treatment. Keeps Class 17 property at a 0.9% taxable valuation rate, extends qualifying construction windows, includes dedicated communications infrastructure and certain onsite generation/storage, requires school equalization mills in TIF districts, and limits sales of power produced by a qualified data center to utilities or cooperatives to cost of production.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; fiscal
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** 2025-05-13
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://bearbeta.legmt.gov/bills/v1/bills/findBySessionIdAndDraftNumber?sessionId=2&draftNumber=LC3009>)

### HB877 / LC2604

- **Policy ID:** `mt-hb877-lc2604`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. John Fitzpatrick; R
- **Status:** Died in process (tabled in House committee 2025-03-31, taken from table 2025-04-04, missed appropriation bill transmittal deadline 2025-04-09), 2025-05-20
- **Provisions:** The LC2604 draft of the proposed "Montana Data Center Development Act" would have limited commission authority to prohibit utility service to certain customers with average monthly demand of at least 5,000 kW that came into existence after October 1, 2007, while retaining authority over tariffs and regulatory processes. Its no-adverse-impact demonstration applies to a distinct class of older customers. Critics described the bill as reducing PSC oversight. The bill died in process; later bill versions were not independently checked.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; statewide
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://bearbeta.legmt.gov/bills/v1/bills/findBySessionIdAndDraftNumber?sessionId=2&draftNumber=LC2604>)

### HJ46 / LC0933

- **Policy ID:** `mt-hj46-lc0933`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Tom Millett; R
- **Status:** Passed House 2025-04-16; tabled in Senate committee 2025-04-24; died in standing committee 2025-05-22
- **Provisions:** Failed HJ46.1 study resolution would have requested an interim committee, statutory committee or staff study of data-center effects on electric adequacy, reliability, affordability and safety; ratepayer costs and regulatory safeguards; load management; bonding or other mitigation of stranded utility investment; distinct utility customer classification; ground/surface-water demand; economic, jobs, tax and housing-affordability impacts; and related high-load industrial topics. It proposed committee review of staff findings and reporting to the 70th Legislature. It did not impose a development moratorium, and its study directions were not adopted through this failed resolution.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; statewide
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** Failed proposal: all study aspects, including presentation and review, would have concluded prior to September 15, 2026, with final results reported to the 70th Legislature. This was a proposed study schedule, not an operative restriction endpoint or proof a study occurred.
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://bearbeta.legmt.gov/docs/v1/documents/getBillText?legislatureOrdinal=69&sessionOrdinal=20251&billType=HJ&billNumber=46>)

### SB212 / LC0292

- **Policy ID:** `mt-sb212-lc0292`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Daniel Zolnikov; R
- **Status:** Signed by Governor 2025-04-16, Chapter 150 assigned 2025-04-17
- **Provisions:** Right to Compute Act. Enrolled section 3 limits government restrictions infringing property/free-expression rights to those demonstrably necessary and narrowly tailored to a compelling government interest. Section 4 requires a reasonable risk-management policy after deploying a critical AI system controlling critical infrastructure; a plan prepared under federal requirements constitutes compliance. Section 7(2)(d) includes prevention or abatement of common-law nuisances created by physical datacenter infrastructure within compelling government interests. This is not a moratorium or blanket exemption from regulation. Later amendments, implementation and current force remain unverified.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; statewide
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** 2025-04-16
- **End condition and limitations:** Enrolled section 10 provides effect on passage and approval; April 16, 2025 is derived from that clause and the retained official governor-signature event. No sunset is specified in the reviewed enrolled act. Later amendments and present force were not checked.
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://archive.legmt.gov/content/Sessions/69th/Contractor_index/CH0150.pdf>)
